Module 02 · Workbook

Workbook: weekly priority system

Observe one week, choose three priorities, protect focus blocks, and define evidence of progress.

Journey outcomeDeliver a short activity log, three justified priorities, a protected calendar, and a review with decisions for the next week.
StartMasterclass
For teams

Make the work that deserves attention visible.

A full calendar does not prove progress. Without explicit criteria, urgent work displaces important work. Missing agreements also scatter team attention.

What you will gain

Leave with defensible priorities, protected time, and a simple way to review progress.

How to proceed

Diagnose, decide, block, execute, and review. Each step leaves an observable artifact.

What to verify

Deliver a short activity log, three justified priorities, a protected calendar, and a review with decisions for the next week.

Build my system

Repeat the system weekly and change one rule when evidence reveals recurring friction.

00 · How to use this workbook

How to use this workbook

Start in class, deepen through practice, and consolidate only with reviewable evidence.

  1. 01

    Frame the caseState the case, desired result and evidence you want to observe.

  2. 02

    Prepare the inputsGather what is needed, acknowledge boundaries and use the three preparation prompts.

  3. 03

    Work in classComplete the essential practice and retain initial evidence.

  4. 04

    Go deeperOpen each detail to review actions, criteria, examples and connections.

  5. 05

    Consolidate and transferMeet the criterion, review the evidence and test the practice in another context.

Orientation

The team week as a system

Align priorities, owners, reviewers, dependencies and rights before testing a shared rule.

Use case
A team with real deliveries and coordination.
You are ready when
A sponsor, exercise owner and permission to review agreed records exist.

Inputs

  • Authorized shared calendar
  • Deliveries and owners
  • Dependencies and exceptions
  • Data access rules
Define your case

Define your case

Write only what is needed to frame the practice. These fields are neither saved nor sent.

00 · Before you begin

Before you begin

01

Prerequisites

  • A sponsor, exercise owner and permission to review agreed records exist.
02

Inputs

  • Authorized shared calendar
  • Deliveries and owners
  • Dependencies and exceptions
  • Data access rules
03

Limits

  • Work with a bounded, authorized case.
  • Do not include personal, confidential or restricted data.
  • Stop when evidence, permission or an accountable reviewer is missing.
01–03 · Workbook

Observe one week, choose three priorities, protect focus blocks, and define evidence of progress.

01 · In class

Prepare the team week

Align records, rights and ownership.

1

Week inventory

Build a baseline before changing the system. Bound shared records and their custody.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • Collect calendar and task records.
  • Record blocks, context switches and outputs.
  • Name the record custodian and people with access.

Quality criteria

  • Covers at least five days or the available period.
  • Separates activity, duration and output.
  • Record custodian and permissions are documented.
Produces
One real-week log for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: Monday 9:00–10:00 meeting; output: decision still pending.
Avoid
Do not reconstruct the week from memory when records exist. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
Which part of the week is still invisible? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Classify the work by value type.
Prompts · prompt-01
2

Value map

Separate useful work, support, coordination and reaction. Align classification with affected areas.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • Label each block with one category.
  • Mark uncertainty where context is missing.
  • Assign a reviewer for disputed categories.

Quality criteria

  • Every category has a reason.
  • Ambiguous cases remain marked.
  • Disputed categories have a reviewer and pending decision.
Produces
Activity value map for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: Prepare delivery = value; coordinate access = necessary support.
Avoid
Do not call all non-delivery work noise. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
Which category takes more space than expected? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Use the map to locate attention leaks.
Prompts · prompt-02
3

Main frictions

Select the two frictions that most alter results. Turn observed frictions into concrete responsibilities.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • Group similar interruptions.
  • Describe trigger, response and consequence.
  • Name the owner of each friction and related dependency.

Quality criteria

  • Each friction cites a fact.
  • Avoid assigning motives to other people.
  • Each friction has an owner and identified dependency.
Produces
Two evidence-backed frictions for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: Unruled messages: four context switches and one moved delivery.
Avoid
Temporal association does not prove causation. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
Which friction can you change without external authority? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Turn the diagnosis into three results.
Prompts · prompt-01
02 · Deepening

Practise shared decisions

Agree criteria, dependencies and blocks.

1

Weekly results

Write three bounded, verifiable results. Write results the sponsor can accept.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • State the definition of done.
  • Declare what is out of scope.
  • Assign the result owner and agreed backup.

Quality criteria

  • Every result is observable.
  • Every boundary prevents scope drift.
  • Each result has an accepted owner and backup.
Produces
Three candidate results for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: Deliver a reviewable draft with five cited sources.
Avoid
Do not use “work on” or “make progress” as the finish condition. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
Which result serves the immediate purpose most? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Compare the results with shared criteria.
Prompts · prompt-03
2

Priority test

Rank results with explicit criteria. Validate the order with those managing dependencies.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • Compare impact, real urgency and effort.
  • Add dependency, risk and missing data.
  • Validate dependencies and risk with those able to resolve them.

Quality criteria

  • The same criteria apply to all results.
  • Ties expose the trade-off.
  • Risks have a reviewer and escalation path.
Produces
Priority matrix for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: Result A: high impact, dependency cleared, medium risk.
Avoid
Do not treat a score as an automatic truth. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
What fact could change the order? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Reserve time for the selected priorities.
Prompts · prompt-04
3

Protected calendar

Turn priorities into executable blocks. Coordinate blocks with other people’s commitments.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • Reserve blocks with purpose and output.
  • Add preparation and definition of done.
  • Align each block with its owner and dependent teams.

Quality criteria

  • Every priority has assigned time.
  • The calendar keeps realistic margin.
  • Blocks respect shared commitments and dependencies.
Produces
Protected weekly calendar for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: Tuesday 9:00–10:30: draft; output: reviewable version.
Avoid
Do not fill every free slot or ignore fixed commitments. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
Which block needs prior preparation? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Define the interruption response.
Prompts · prompt-05
03 · Consolidation

Transfer a team rule

Review evidence and govern adoption.

1

Execution record

Compare the plan with what happened. Share status without exceeding agreed permissions.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • Mark blocks completed, moved or cancelled.
  • Record the evidence produced.
  • Give status to the reviewer without exposing others’ data.

Quality criteria

  • Every status has evidence.
  • A deviation retains its context.
  • Status can be reviewed under current rights.
Produces
Plan-versus-execution record for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: Block completed; partial output; one source still needs review.
Avoid
Do not confuse attendance in a block with a completed result. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
What decision became possible because of the record? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Explain one deviation without automatic justification.
Prompts · prompt-07
2

Deviation analysis

Explain one difference between plan and facts. Separate operating failures from external dependencies.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • Describe fact, condition and response.
  • Separate personal control from external dependency.
  • Separate the external dependency from the internal operating change.

Quality criteria

  • The explanation uses facts.
  • The action addresses the observed condition.
  • The deviation separates internal owner and external dependency.
Produces
Deviation note for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: The block started late because input was not ready; prepare it the day before.
Avoid
Do not turn one case into a universal rule. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
What alternative was under your control? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Choose one rule to keep and one to adjust.
Prompts · prompt-07
3

Rule for next week

Turn review into a testable adjustment. Prepare a rule that can be reviewed before scaling.

Go deeperQuality criteria

How to apply it

  • Keep one useful practice.
  • Change one friction and schedule review.
  • Define sponsor, adoption gate and review date.

Quality criteria

  • The rule is concrete and bounded.
  • A review date and evidence are defined.
  • The rule has a sponsor and adoption condition.
Produces
Reviewable weekly rule for the team with ownership
Example
Synthetic team example: Prepare inputs the day before; review on Friday.
Avoid
Do not change many rules at once if that hides what helped. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
Reflect
What evidence will keep or remove the rule? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
Connection
Add the rule to the visible system.
Prompts · prompt-07
Transfer

Repeat the system weekly and change one rule when evidence reveals recurring friction.

Turn a real week into a visible priority system: three justified outcomes, protected blocks, and a final review.

Consolidation criterion

Transferable

Another team can adopt the rule because roles, exceptions and review are explicit.

Expected evidence
Two comparable weeks, a team-level record and one documented adoption decision.
Review
At the end of the next week and before extending the rule to another team.

Pilot one rule with the team for another week

Repeat the cycle with one agreed change so its effect can be attributed.

  • Name owner, reviewer and affected teams.
  • Confirm rights, dependencies and exception path.
  • Review adoption and evidence before expanding.
Evidence
Two comparable weeks, a team-level record and one documented adoption decision.
Review
At the end of the next week and before extending the rule to another team.
Closing rubric

Closing rubric

1

Initial

The team records activity, but shared criteria, accountable roles or evidence are still missing.

2

Applicable

Priorities, protected blocks, accountable roles and shared review connect to evidence.

3

Transferable

Another team can adopt the rule because roles, exceptions and review are explicit.
